title: William of Rubruck from Constantinople to Karakorum and back, 1253-55
summary: A Flemish Franciscan sent by Louis IX to the Mongols crossed the Black Sea to the Crimea, then the steppe to Batu on the Volga and 9,000 km further to the court of Mongke at Karakorum. He came home by the Caucasus, Armenia, Anatolia and Cyprus to Tripoli in 1255. His report to Louis is the best Western account of the Mongols, with dated stages and a long debate at court.

legs.source: Rubruck: from Constantinople by sea to Soldaia, where he landed on 21 May 1253
Rubruck: left Soldaia about 1 June with carts and oxen, and crossed the Don before 22 June
legs.doubt: Where he crossed the Don is not placed; the pin is at its mouth.

legs.source: Rubruck: stage by stage across the steppe to Sartaq, reached on 31 July
legs.doubt: Rubruck puts Sartaq's camp three days from the Volga; the pin is one reading of that.

legs.source: Rubruck: three days east to Batu, on the Volga, whom he reached on 5 August
Rubruck: from 15 September to 1 November across the Kangly steppe, crossing the Jaik (Ural), and into the Saracen town of Kinchat on 8 November
legs.doubt: The route across the steppe is not given stage by stage; Kinchat is Kenjek, on the Syr Darya, and its place is a rough one.

legs.source: Rubruck: east along the mountains, the Chu valley and the plain by the lake, to the market town of Cailac, where he rested twelve days
legs.doubt: Rubruck did not reach Talas, which was six days off his road; the pin at Cailac (Qayaligh) is only roughly placed.

legs.source: Rubruck: over mountains and a plain 'vast as a sea', reaching Mongke's court on 27 December 1253
legs.doubt: The camp was a tent city that moved; where it stood in winter is not known.

legs.source: Rubruck: followed the court to Karakorum, where he arrived on 7 May 1254
Rubruck: left Mongke's court in July and reached Batu on 16 September 1254
legs.doubt: Rubruck does not describe the road home stage by stage; the line is a broad brush across the steppe.

legs.source: Rubruck: left Batu on All Saints (1 November) and went south to the Iron Gate
legs.doubt: He dates his leaving and arriving but names no stops on the steppe.

legs.source: Rubruck: the Iron Gate, Samaron, Shamakhi, the Mughan plain and up the Araxes past Baachu's camp to Nakhchivan, where he kept Christmas
Rubruck: left Nakhchivan on 13 January 1255 and was at Ani on 2 February
Rubruck: up the Araxes to its head, down the Euphrates through the earthquake country by Erzincan, and at Sivas in Holy Week
Rubruck: Caesarea of Cappadocia on 4 April and Iconium on 19 April
Rubruck: to Korykos on the Armenian coast, which he reached on 4 May, and then to the king's father at Sis and the port of Ayas
Rubruck: from Ayas across to Cyprus, which he entered on 16 June, and Nicosia
Rubruck: with the Provincial from Nicosia to Antioch, where they kept the feast of Saints Peter and Paul on 29 June
Rubruck: from Antioch to Tripoli, where the chapter ordered him to stay at Acre and not return to the king

events.label: Soldaia, May 1253
events.text: Merchants had gone ahead of him saying that envoys from the Holy Land were coming, though he had preached in Saint Sophia on Palm Sunday that he was nobody's envoy, only a friar going among unbelievers by his order's rule. At Soldaia they warned him to speak guardedly.

events.label: Sartaq's camp, 31 July 1253
events.text: Rubruck gave Sartaq Louis IX's letter and was questioned about it, then sent on to Batu, who sent him on again to Mongke.
events.doubt: Rubruck dates the arrival but not the place; the mark stands where one reading puts it.

events.label: Mongke's court, January 1254
events.text: He reached the Great Khan's tents on 27 December and was taken to court on 3 or 4 January 1254. Nestorian priests there took the clean-shaven friars for Buddhists, and asked which way they prayed.
events.doubt: The winter camp was a moving tent city; the mark is a guess at its place.

events.label: A debate at Karakorum, May 1254
events.text: On the Sunday before Pentecost Christians, Muslims and Buddhists argued before the Khan's secretaries; Mongke had asked each to write down what it believed. At court Rubruck met Guillaume Boucher, a French goldsmith who made the drink-flowing silver tree at the Khan's feast.

events.label: Christmas at Nakhchivan, 1254
events.text: On the way back, he kept Christmas in one of the last two Armenian churches of a city that once had eighty. A bishop and twelve monks came down from the hills to bury the church's priest, and Rubruck found a Dominican, Friar Bernard of Catalonia, there.
